title: Selecting language and logo version

location.series: City of Helsinki live visual identity guidelines

slide_intent: Balance multilingual recognition with visual clarity so residents can identify a city service without competing signatures.
strategic_value: A bilingual signature or deliberately separated versions can acknowledge Helsinki’s audiences while keeping each view clear.
demonstration: This expanded webpage section explains language selection, defines one view–one logo and compares incorrect and correct A4, wall and fence arrangements.
practical_value: Select the language version and count visible signatures within the viewer’s actual field of view.

content_islands.name: Language rules
content_islands.spec: Open with audience and language guidance.

content_islands.name: View definition
content_islands.spec: Define a view through sides, time and physical distance.

content_islands.name: Arrangement examples
content_islands.spec: Place numbered A4, wall and fence diagrams with their explanatory key.

content_islands.name: Support
content_islands.spec: End with contact guidance for uncertain cases.

ingredient.name: Language versions within one view
ingredient.role: Acknowledge audience language without multiplying competing marks.
ingredient.application: Use Helsinki for Finnish/English/international, Helsingfors for Swedish; use a bilingual mark or equal-height separated marks for multilingual resident communication.
ingredient.scope: One view normally contains one logo; approximately five metres is contextual separation guidance, not a universal minimum; interview logo backdrops are an exception.

reference_purposes.Intent: The source introduces the one-view rule explicitly for clarity.
reference_purposes.Application: Numbered arrangements show bilingual signatures, different sides and sufficient separation.
reference_purposes.Constraint: Resident-facing bilingual or multilingual communications must include Swedish; normally one version per view, with interview backdrop exception.
